title: A Noetherian complete local ring is a G-ring
statement: Let $(S,\mathfrak n)$ be a Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] local ring which is complete, i.e. $\mathfrak n$-adically complete [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]: the canonical map $S\to\varprojlim_nS/\mathfrak n^n$ to its $\mathfrak n$-adic completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] is bijective. Then $S$ is a G-ring [def-weil-pbc-g-ring]: for every prime ideal $\mathfrak q\subset S$ the completion map $S_{\mathfrak q}\to(S_{\mathfrak q})^\wedge$ is a regular ring map.

source.place: Proposition Tag 07PS (more-algebra-proposition-Noetherian-complete-G-ring, line 12356); complete local ring: algebra.tex Definition Tag 0324

proof.text: (Reduction to formal fibres of the quotients $S/\mathfrak q$.) $S$ is Noetherian, so by [lem-weil-pbc-g-ring-check-pairs-of-primes] it suffices to show, for every pair of primes $\mathfrak q\subseteq\mathfrak p$ of $S$, with $B=S/\mathfrak q$ and $\bar{\mathfrak p}=\mathfrak p/\mathfrak q$, that the $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$-algebra $(B_{\bar{\mathfrak p}})^\wedge\otimes_B\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ is Noetherian and geometrically regular over $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$, where $\kappa(\mathfrak q)=S_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak qS_{\mathfrak q}=B_{(0)}$ is the fraction field of the domain $B$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Noetherianity holds in any case: $B_{\bar{\mathfrak p}}$ is Noetherian (every ideal of a quotient or of a localization of the Noetherian ring $S$ is the image, resp. the extension, of an ideal of $S$ [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]), hence $(B_{\bar{\mathfrak p}})^\wedge$ is Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian] and so is its fibre ring $(B_{\bar{\mathfrak p}})^\wedge\otimes_B\kappa(\mathfrak q)=(B_{\bar{\mathfrak p}})^\wedge\otimes_{B_{\bar{\mathfrak p}}}\kappa((0))$ [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-noetherian]. It remains to prove geometric regularity.

source.place: Proposition Tag 07PS (proposition-Noetherian-complete-G-ring, line 12356), proof, first paragraph: 'By Lemma 07PN it suffices to check that B = A/q has geometrically regular formal fibres over the minimal prime (0) of B'

proof.text: (Reduction to a complete local domain.) Since $\mathfrak q\subseteq\mathfrak n$ is a proper ideal, $B=S/\mathfrak q$ is a Noetherian local ring which is complete with respect to its maximal ideal $\mathfrak n/\mathfrak q$ [lem-weil-pbc-complete-local-quotient], and it is a domain as $\mathfrak q$ is prime. Hence, applied to $A=B$ and $P=\bar{\mathfrak p}$, it suffices to prove: $(\dagger)$ if $(A,\mathfrak m_A)$ is a Noetherian local domain which is $\mathfrak m_A$-adically complete [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring], with fraction field $K=A_{(0)}=\kappa((0))$, then for every prime $P$ of $A$ the $K$-algebra $(A_P)^\wedge\otimes_AK$ is geometrically regular over $K$ [def-weil-pbc-g-ring].

source.place: Proposition Tag 07PS, proof, first paragraph ('Thus we may assume that A is a domain and it suffices to check the condition for the formal fibres over the minimal prime (0) of A'); quotient: Algebra Lemma Tag 0325 (lemma-quotient-complete-local, line 44811)

proof.text: (A regular subring.) Let $A$, $P$, $K$ be as in $(\dagger)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-complete-local-domain-finite-over-regular] there is a subring $A_0\subseteq A$ which is a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme] (in particular Noetherian), complete with respect to its maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_0=\mathfrak m_A\cap A_0$, such that $A$ is a finitely generated $A_0$-module and $A_0$ is isomorphic to $k[[X_1,\ldots,X_d]]$ for a field $k$ or to $\Lambda[[X_1,\ldots,X_d]]$ for a Cohen ring $\Lambda$. As a subring of the domain $A$, $A_0$ is a domain; let $K_0=(A_0)_{(0)}=\kappa((0))$ be its fraction field [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Put $P_0=P\cap A_0$, a prime of $A_0$; the zero ideal of $A$ contracts to the zero ideal of $A_0$. Being a finite module, $A$ is in particular a finitely generated $A_0$-algebra.

source.place: Proposition Tag 07PS, proof, second paragraph ('We can choose a subring A_0 in A which is a regular complete local ring such that A is finite over A_0 ... Moreover, we may assume that A_0 is a power series ring over a field or a Cohen ring'); Algebra Lemma Tag 032D (line 45065)

proof.text: (Passing to $A_0$.) The map $A_0\to A$ is quasi-finite at $P$ [pqf-def-quasifinite]: the fibre ring $C=A\otimes_{A_0}\kappa(P_0)$ is spanned over the field $\kappa(P_0)$ by the images of finitely many $A_0$-module generators of $A$, so $\dim_{\kappa(P_0)}C<\infty$; for every prime $Q$ of $C$ the domain $C/Q$ is a finite-dimensional $\kappa(P_0)$-algebra, hence a field (multiplication by a nonzero element is injective, hence surjective), so every prime of $C$ is maximal; distinct maximal ideals $Q_1,\ldots,Q_r$ give a surjection $C\to\prod_iC/Q_i$ (Chinese remainder theorem), so $r\le\dim C$; thus $\operatorname{Spec}C$ is finite with all points closed, hence discrete, and the point of $P$ is isolated. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-formal-fibre-quasi-finite-ascent] to the Noetherian rings $R=A_0$, $R'=A$ and the primes $\mathfrak q'=(0)\subseteq\mathfrak p'=P$ of $A$, lying over $\mathfrak q=(0)\subseteq\mathfrak p=P_0$ of $A_0$ (Step 3): since $\kappa((0))=K$ in $A$ and $\kappa((0))=K_0$ in $A_0$, if $(\ddagger)$ the $K_0$-algebra $((A_0)_{P_0})^\wedge\otimes_{A_0}K_0$ is geometrically regular over $K_0$, then $(A_P)^\wedge\otimes_AK$ is geometrically regular over $K$, which is $(\dagger)$. So it suffices to prove $(\ddagger)$.

source.place: Proposition Tag 07PS, proof, second paragraph ('By Lemma 07PP we see that it suffices to prove the result for A_0'); More on Algebra Lemma Tag 07PP (lemma-G-ring-goes-up-quasi-finite, line 12214), item (1); finite implies quasi-finite: Algebra Definition 00PL with Lemma 00PM (fibres finite over kappa(p)), written out here

proof.text: (The fibre is regular.) Put $C=((A_0)_{P_0})^\wedge$ and $F=C\otimes_{A_0}K_0$. The localization $(A_0)_{P_0}$ of the regular local ring $A_0$ is a regular local ring [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-localization], so its completion $C$, a Noetherian local ring [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian] [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-local-ring], is a regular local ring [lem-weil-pbc-completion-regular-local], and by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-localization] again $C$ is a regular ring: every localization $C_Q$ at a prime $Q$ is a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Since $K_0=W_0^{-1}A_0$ with $W_0=A_0\setminus\{0\}$, $F=W^{-1}C$ is the localization of $C$ at the image $W$ of $W_0$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Hence $F$ is Noetherian (ideals of $W^{-1}C$ are extended from $C$ [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]), its primes are the $W^{-1}Q$ with $Q$ a prime of $C$ disjoint from $W$, and $F_{W^{-1}Q}\cong C_Q$ is a regular local ring. So $F$ is a regular ring.

source.place: Proposition Tag 07PS, proof, third paragraph ('Since A is regular the localizations A_p are regular ... Hence the completions A_p^ are regular, see Lemma 07NY. Hence the fibre A_p^ (x)_A K is, as a localization of A_p^, also regular'); Algebra Lemma Tag 0AFS (line 27126) and Definition Tag 00OD; More on Algebra Lemma Tag 07NY (line 10668)

proof.text: (Characteristic $0$.) Suppose $K_0$ has characteristic $0$. Then the only finite purely inseparable extension of $K_0$ is $K_0$ itself [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension], and $K_0\otimes_{K_0}F=F$ is regular by Step 5; so $F$ is geometrically regular over $K_0$ by definition [def-weil-pbc-g-ring], which is $(\ddagger)$.

source.place: Proposition Tag 07PS, proof, third paragraph ('Thus we are done if the characteristic of K is 0'); geometric regularity by finite purely inseparable extensions: Algebra Lemma Tag 0381 (2) and Definition Tag 0382 (lines 47104, 47151)

proof.text:
(Characteristic $p>0$.) Suppose $K_0$ has characteristic $p>0$. Then $A_0
ot\cong\Lambda[[X_1,\ldots,X_d]]$ for a Cohen ring $\Lambda$: such a ring contains $\Lambda$, a domain which is not a field and whose maximal ideal is generated by a prime number $\ell$, so $\ell
e0$ in $\Lambda$; if $\Lambda$ had characteristic a prime $r$, then $r=\ell$ would give $\ell=0$, and $r
e\ell$ would make $\ell$ a unit ($1=ar+b\ell$ with $a,b\in\mathbf Z$), contradicting $\ell$ in the maximal ideal; so $\Lambda$, hence $A_0$ and $K_0$, would have characteristic $0$. Hence (Step 3) there is a ring isomorphism $\sigma:k[[X_1,\ldots,X_d]]\xrightarrow{\sim}A_0$ for a field $k$, which has characteristic $p$ since $k\subseteq A_0\subseteq K_0$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-helper-g-ring-char-p] with $n=d$, $m=0$ and the prime $\sigma^{-1}(P_0)$; transported along $\sigma$ (which induces isomorphisms of the localizations, completions and fraction fields), it says that $((A_0)_{P_0})^\wedge\otimes_{A_0}K_0$ is geometrically regular over $K_0$, i.e. $(\ddagger)$. Together with Step 6, $(\ddagger)$ holds in all cases, hence $(\dagger)$ by Step 4, hence by Steps 2 and 1 every formal fibre in [lem-weil-pbc-g-ring-check-pairs-of-primes] is geometrically regular and $S$ is a G-ring [def-weil-pbc-g-ring].

The brief's candidate tags 07PT (this item's user), 07C0, 07PQ, 07PU are not used by 07PS; 07PP is used in its item (1), not the quotient item (3) of lem-weil-pbc-g-ring-quotient. New unsplit nodes: lem-weil-pbc-g-ring-check-pairs-of-primes (07PN), lem-weil-pbc-complete-local-quotient (0325), lem-weil-pbc-complete-local-domain-finite-over-regular (032D), lem-weil-pbc-formal-fibre-quasi-finite-ascent (07PP(1)), lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-localization (0AFS), lem-weil-pbc-completion-regular-local (07NY), lem-weil-pbc-helper-g-ring-char-p (07PR); all searched with LeanSearch, Loogle/LeanFinder and grep, none in Mathlib (Mathlib has IsRegularLocalRing/IsRegularRing and Algebra.QuasiFiniteAt but no Serre localization theorem, no regularity of completions, no Cohen structure theorem, no formal fibres).
